evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with an acute gout flare: first-line NSAID, colchicine or short-course oral corticosteroid, renal and interaction cautions, second-line options and when to start urate-lowering therapy, using NICE NG219 and a UK hospital same-day emergency care guideline.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG219 gives no doses; doses are from one undated hospital guideline (University Hospitals Birmingham same-day emergency care) without page numbers.
HLA-B*5801 testing, azathioprine interaction and the maximum colchicine dose are not mentioned in the sources opened.
NICE notes that NSAIDs, colchicine and short-course oral corticosteroids are off-label for some indications (as of June 2022).
No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Rheumatology/Infectious Diseases guideline was opened.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: NICE offers an NSAID, colchicine or a short course of an oral corticosteroid as first-line flare treatment, chosen by comorbidities, co-prescriptions and preference. A proton pump inhibitor is added if an NSAID is used. Intra-articular or intramuscular corticosteroid is used if NSAIDs and colchicine are contraindicated, not tolerated or ineffective. Interleukin-1 inhibitors are reserved for failure of NSAIDs, colchicine and corticosteroids and need rheumatology referral first.

clinicalManagement.title: Choose first-line flare drug
actions: Offer an NSAID, colchicine or a short oral corticosteroid by comorbidities, co-prescriptions and preference; add a proton pump inhibitor with an NSAID.

clinicalManagement.title: Dose by kidney function and interactions
actions: Avoid NSAIDs in the elderly or eGFR under 30; reduce colchicine in eGFR 10 to 50; consider colchicine reduction with interacting drugs.

clinicalManagement.title: Second line
actions: Intra-articular or intramuscular corticosteroid; interleukin-1 inhibitor only after rheumatology referral.

clinicalManagement.title: Plan long-term control
clinicalManagement.timeframe: 2 to 4 weeks after the flare settles
actions: Discuss urate-lowering therapy with everyone who has had a flare; see the urate-lowering therapy topic.

adjustments: Avoid in elderly patients or eGFR under 30.
contraindications: eGFR under 30; elderly patients; NSAID contraindications such as ulcer or cardiovascular disease per comorbidity review.
